title: I don't understand
canDo: say you don't understand and ask for help

dialogue.setting: Priya is at a pharmacy in Gatineau, Quebec. The pharmacist, Mr. Roy, speaks quickly.

lines.speaker: M. Roy
lines.fr: Bonjour ! Votre carte d'assurance maladie, s'il vous plaît.
lines.en: Hello! Your health insurance card, please.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.fr: Pardon ? Je ne comprends pas. Pouvez-vous répéter, s'il vous plaît ?
lines.en: Sorry? I don't understand. Can you repeat, please?

lines.speaker: M. Roy
lines.en: Thank you. Do you speak English?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.fr: Oui. Je parle un peu français. Comment dit-on « prescription » en français ?
lines.en: Yes. I speak a little French. How do you say "prescription" in French?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.en: A prescription. Thank you very much!

vocabulary.note: Asks someone to repeat. Pardon on its own also means "excuse me".

vocabulary.en: How do you say … in French?

vocabulary.canadianNote: Quebec's health card, issued by the RAMQ. Other provinces have their own cards.

vocabulary.note: A woman pharmacist is la pharmacienne.

grammar.title: ne … pas as a fixed phrase
explanation: To say "not", French puts ne before the verb and pas after it: je comprends means "I understand", je ne comprends pas means "I don't understand".
For now, learn je ne comprends pas and je ne sais pas as fixed phrases. You'll use ne … pas with other verbs later.
In everyday speech, people often drop the ne: je comprends pas, je sais pas. Learn to recognise it, but use the full form yourself.

examples.fr: Je ne parle pas bien français.

explanation: In everyday French, you can turn a sentence into a yes-or-no question just by raising your voice at the end. The words stay the same.
Vous parlez anglais, with the voice going down, is a statement. Vous parlez anglais ?, with the voice going up, is a question.
Questions that start with a question word, like Comment dit-on … ?, often go down at the end instead.

examples.en: Do you speak English? (voice goes up)

exercises.prompt: The cashier speaks too fast. What do you say?
You want the French word for "form". What do you ask?

drills.en: How do you say "form" in French?

You caught a few words, but the agent spoke too fast. What do you ask?
